page.layout: Running head at top, with page number at left. Two coin medallions (woodcut illustrations) side by side at top, their legends printed around the rims. Below them one column of text, two paragraphs. No margin notes, no notes under the text, no catchword or signature.

main_text.p: LICINIVS in Dacia natus, mortuo Severo, consors Imperij factus est à Maximiano Galerio, anno mundi 4270. à Christo nato 308 idque ob virtutem rei militaris. Prius Illyriis, post Orieti præfuit: parentes habuit agricolas, ipse rusticus & barbarus rusticis & agrariis æquus, at crudelis etiā in Galerij liberos. literarum hostis fuit infensissimus, quas venenum ac pestem appellabat: quippe qui harū rudis ac expers adeò esset, ut ne nomen quidē suum decretis subscribere posset. Christianis adversabatur, nec destitit, sæpius rogatus ab Constantino: quare Constantinus contra illum vires Gallicanas & Italicas iure expertus est. primis congressibus in Pannonia victus, concessit in Macedoniam Licinius: ubi vires reparantē, Constantinus iterum adoritur, fugat in Asiam. Tandē navalibus & terrestribus præliis victus, mittitur Thessalonicē, ut privatus cum uxore degat. Sed cum rebelles adhuc animos homo ille vecors retineret, interfici iubetur. vixit an. 60. imperavit 14. Constantino imperante. laudatur quòd aulicorum insolētiam mirè compescuerit, tineas foricésque palatinos eos appellans. Pomp.Læt.

CONSTANTIA, vxor fuit Licinij, ac soror Constantini, quæ (ut fertur) fratrem adiit, pro Imperio mariti rogavit, deinde pro titulo tantum, nec impetravit: tandem pro salute rogans, impetravit. Vide Pomp.Læt. hæc Licinium iuniore peperit, quem Constantinus Magnus Cæsarem creavit.

page.notes: Coin legends are printed in the woodcut medallions; the left one is read as IMP.LIC.LICINIANVS.P.F.AVG. and the right one as CONSTANTIA.VXOR.M.IVL.LIC., both uncertain at the small scale. Heavy blur at the bottom of the page; no legible text there. Printed u/v spellings were normalised to u for vowels and v for consonants throughout. Long s rendered as s.
